column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the process for reassigning supplier contacts where the outgoing contact does not proactively update the profile themselves — can procurement or admin force a reassignment?

column3: The supplier profile shall carry current insurance certificate and sanctions-screening status, shared with the Tender Portal onboarding checks.
column7: Given a supplier profile, when it is viewed by an authorised internal user, then current insurance certificate status and the latest sanctions-screening result and date are displayed, and the same data drives the Tender Portal checks.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm this requirement's scope is contingent on the FR-0185 (insurance OCR) and FR-0180 (sanctions screening) decisions requested elsewhere, since it displays their output on the supplier profile.

column3: The system shall automatically create one evaluation record per supplier that actually submitted a response, excluding non-respondents from scoring and reporting without manual removal.
column7: Given a closed tender with invited suppliers who did not submit, when the evaluation is opened, then evaluation records exist only for actual respondents and no manual removal step is required.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the point at which a supplier is deemed to have 'submitted a response' for evaluation-record creation — any partial upload, or a completed and locked submission only.

column3: Evaluators shall operate in role-scoped, isolated views, seeing only the bid files they are authorised to assess for their assigned stream; technical evaluators shall be blocked from viewing commercial pricing data to prevent financial bias.
column7: Given a technical evaluator, when they open a bid, then commercial pricing content is not retrievable through any view, export or search, and the access scope is recorded in the audit trail.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the specific 'assigned evaluation stream' groupings Intuitive Fusion uses (e.g. by lot, by category, by technical/commercial split) so evaluator view isolation can be configured correctly.

column3: The evaluation workflow shall include a mandatory pass/fail compliance gate covering matters such as entity registration, mandatory declarations and insurance limits, with automated checking for missed mandatory requirements and automated clarification requests to suppliers.
column7: Given a submission missing a mandatory requirement, when the compliance gate runs, then the submission is marked fail with the specific deficiency identified, and a clarification request can be issued to the supplier before qualitative scoring begins.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the complete list of mandatory compliance criteria for the pass/fail gate beyond the examples given (entity registration, mandatory declarations, insurance limits).

column3: The system shall support independent, hidden individual qualitative scoring against standardised rubrics, such that an evaluator cannot see other evaluators' scores before consensus.
column7: Given multiple evaluators scoring the same submission, when an evaluator views the scoring screen, then no other evaluator's scores or comments are visible until the consensus stage is opened.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether individual evaluator scores remain permanently hidden from peers after consensus is reached, or whether they become visible for audit/training purposes once the process concludes.

column3: The system shall provide a consensus moderation stage in which the panel chair reviews all individual scores side-by-side, with the system flagging deviations beyond a pre-set variance limit (e.g. a 30% gap between evaluators) for mandatory discussion.
column7: Given individual scores where two evaluators differ by more than the configured variance limit, when the chair opens consensus, then the deviation is flagged and consensus cannot be locked until the flagged item is discussed and a rationale recorded.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the 30% variance-flag threshold shown as an example is the required default for Intuitive Fusion, or specify a different variance trigger for mandatory consensus discussion.

column3: The system shall support both numeric scoring and simple ranking, with ranking available as a configurable option for low-value/low-risk arrangements; ranking shall be computed automatically from consensus scores blended with normalised commercial Total Cost of Ownership and project weightings.
column7: Given a low-value arrangement configured for ranking, when consensus is locked, then a ranking is computed automatically from consensus scores, normalised TCO and the configured weightings, and the calculation is shown.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the value/risk threshold below which simple ranking (rather than full scoring) may be used, consistent with the Simple/Complex threshold requested at FR-0025.

column3: The system shall support multi-stage evaluations, with each stage able to shortlist one or more suppliers before the next stage is run, and scores retained for all rounds.
column7: Given a multi-stage evaluation, when a stage concludes, then shortlisted suppliers progress to the next stage, and the completed stage's scores remain retrievable and reportable.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether scores from an earlier evaluation stage may be referenced/weighted in a later stage's consensus, or whether each stage's scoring is entirely independent.

column3: The platform shall provide a negotiation and Best and Final Offer workspace supporting audited clarification requests with response deadlines, and a controlled mini-tendering cycle for updated pricing that preserves the original bid history.
column7: Given a BAFO round, when updated pricing is submitted, then the original bid remains intact and separately retrievable, and every clarification request and response is timestamped against its deadline.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether a Best and Final Offer (BAFO) round is expected to be a standard, configurable stage for complex procurements, or an exception process used only occasionally.

column3: The system shall generate AI-assisted negotiation recommendations (e.g. a suggested discount percentage, or specific clauses/indemnities to negotiate) based on submitted pricing and terms versus category/market benchmarks.
column7: Given submitted pricing and terms, when negotiation recommendations are requested, then the system presents specific recommended levers with the benchmark basis stated, clearly labelled as AI-generated and requiring human judgement.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the source of the 'category/market benchmarks' the AI should compare submitted pricing against — in-house historical data, a licensed third-party benchmark, or both.

column3: Before vendor names or bid documents are exposed, evaluators shall be required to complete a mandatory conflict-of-interest declaration; a declared conflict shall immediately revoke the evaluator's project access and escalate an alert to the Panel Chair and Probity Advisor.
column7: Given an evaluator who has not completed a COI declaration, when they attempt to open the evaluation, then vendor identities and bid documents are withheld; when a conflict is declared, then project access is revoked immediately and the Panel Chair and Probity Advisor are alerted.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the point at which vendor identities are considered 'exposed' for conflict-of-interest purposes — first viewing of the shortlist, or first viewing of any bid content.

column3: The system shall support an evaluator substitution workflow: on mid-project replacement, the departing evaluator's marks are locked as read-only history, and the incoming evaluator completes a fresh conflict-of-interest declaration before receiving a clean scoring matrix, with panel averages recalculated automatically.
column7: Given an evaluator replaced mid-evaluation, when the substitution is recorded, then the departing evaluator's marks become read-only history, the incoming evaluator must complete a COI declaration before scoring, and panel averages are recalculated without the departing evaluator's scores.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether panel averages should be recalculated retrospectively across all prior scoring stages when a new evaluator joins mid-project, or only prospectively from the point of substitution.

column3: The platform shall provide a read-only Probity Advisor oversight portal for external auditors, scoped to only the procurements the advisor is allocated to, including a system-hold control that can freeze the evaluation workspace on suspected bias or process breach.
column7: Given an external probity advisor allocated to one procurement, when they log in, then only that procurement is visible, all content is read-only, and activating the system hold prevents any further scoring action until released.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether the 'System Hold' safety button is available to internal probity officers as well as external probity advisors, and confirm who is authorised to release a hold once applied.

column3: Scoring, ranking and evaluation commentary shall be capable of being entered in plain language, in addition to structured score entry.
column7: Given an evaluator describing an assessment in plain language, when the entry is saved, then the structured score and commentary fields are populated accordingly and remain user-amendable.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm plain-language scoring entries must still map to a structured numeric score for ranking purposes, or whether narrative-only scoring is acceptable for some workflow tiers.

column3: Evaluation criteria shall be selectable from a pre-populated criteria library, easily amendable, and configurable to be the same or different across evaluation stages.
column7: Given a new evaluation, when criteria are selected, then a pre-populated criteria set is offered, criteria can be added, removed or reworded, and different criteria sets can be applied to different stages.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design; supports the standardised rubrics in FR-054.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether Intuitive Fusion has an existing evaluation criteria library available for initial configuration, or whether Blue Pearl should propose a standard starter library.

column3: The system shall automatically issue conflict-of-interest re-declaration reminders after the tender closes, once supplier identities are known, and shall report which users have not yet declared.
column7: Given a tender that has closed, when the re-declaration cycle runs, then every required declarant receives an automated reminder and a delegate-visible report shows outstanding declarations by name.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design, which also requires the outstanding-declaration view for delegates.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the required cadence of automated conflict-of-interest re-declaration reminders after tender close (e.g. once only, or repeating until declared).

column3: Conflict-of-interest outcomes shall be recorded against a defined set of dispositions — immaterial (remain in role), minor (remain but excluded from assessing the conflicted supplier), or material (removed from the procurement) — decided by the relevant delegate, a more senior officer, or the risk and compliance team.
column7: Given a declared conflict, when a disposition is recorded, then the corresponding access change is applied automatically (no change, supplier-level exclusion, or full removal) and the decision-maker is recorded.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design; extends the COI routing requirement in BRS §4.6.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm who holds authority to determine 'immaterial' versus 'minor' versus 'material' for a declared conflict where it is not obvious — is this always the relevant delegate, or can Risk & Compliance override the delegate's classification?

column3: Where a person is removed from a procurement for a material conflict, the platform shall support nominating a replacement and shall automatically issue the conflict-of-interest declaration request and all other outstanding procurement tasks to that replacement.
column7: Given a participant removed for a material conflict, when a replacement is nominated, then the replacement automatically receives the COI declaration request and the removed participant's outstanding tasks.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design; overlaps FR-061 for evaluators and extends it to delegates, advisors and steering committee members.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm how a replacement evaluator/delegate is selected when someone is removed for a material conflict — is there a defined backup/deputy list, or is this a manual nomination each time?

column3: A probity advisor shall be able to upload, or author in-platform, a probity plan and probity outcomes report, generated to Word or PDF with a profile-based sign-off stamp and a clear audit trail attributing the sign-off to that advisor.
column7: Given a probity advisor authoring an outcomes report in-platform, when they sign it off, then the generated document carries their profile stamp and the audit trail records the advisor identity and timestamp.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether Intuitive Fusion requires the platform-generated probity report stamp to meet a specific format/certification standard (e.g. for court or tribunal admissibility).

column3: The evaluation report shall be auto-populated from the RFx content, supplier submissions and evaluation/consensus outcomes once the tender process concludes, reflecting the evaluation committee's recorded commentary and rationale per supplier.
column7: Given a concluded evaluation, when the report is generated, then RFx content, submission detail, scores and per-supplier committee commentary are populated without manual transcription.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the required level of narrative auto-drafting for evaluation commentary — should the AI draft full paragraphs from evaluator notes, or only compile the evaluators' own verbatim commentary?

column3: On consensus lock, the system shall automatically compile a Sourcing Recommendation Report combining pass/fail compliance logs, scoring distributions, panel justifications and TCO normalisation, and shall output the final value-for-money recommendation.
column7: Given a locked consensus, when the Sourcing Recommendation Report is produced, then it contains the compliance log, score distribution, panel justifications, TCO normalisation and a stated value-for-money recommendation.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the required output format(s) for the compiled Sourcing Recommendation Report — in-platform page, Word, PDF, or all three.

column3: The evaluation report shall be printable, shall carry a timestamp containing all required audit information, and shall be viewable and actionable for review and approval on both desktop and mobile devices.
column7: Given a generated report, when it is printed or exported, then it carries the audit timestamp; and a delegate on a mobile device can review it and record an approval decision.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the specific audit information the evaluation report timestamp must display (e.g. generation date, last-edited date, all signatory dates).

column3: For multi-stage evaluations, the evaluation report shall document the outcomes of each individual stage.
column7: Given a multi-stage evaluation, when the report is generated, then each stage's shortlist, scores and rationale appear as a distinct, identifiable section.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether a single evaluation report documents all stages of a multi-stage evaluation, or whether a separate report is required per stage.

column3: The evaluation report layout shall support drag-and-drop configuration, or a system-provided default template where the customer has none.
column7: Given the report layout designer, when a user arranges and sizes fields, then the saved layout governs the generated report; where no custom layout exists, the system default is used.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether Intuitive Fusion has an existing evaluation report template, or requires the system default template at go-live.

column3: Conflict-of-interest declarations shall be capable of being captured and recorded at the evaluation report stage in the same manner as at the procurement plan stage.
column7: Given the evaluation report stage, when a participant declares a conflict, then it is captured conversationally, recorded against the report, and routed for decision on the same basis as a plan-stage declaration.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm conflict-of-interest declarations at evaluation-report stage are a fresh declaration event, or a carry-forward/confirmation of the plan-stage declaration in FR-0105.

column3: The evaluation report shall include an explicit sign-off/approval step, routed to the delegate holding the appropriate authority for the procurement's value tier, before the report can progress to contract award.
column7: Given an unapproved evaluation report, when contract award is attempted, then progression is blocked until the value-tier-appropriate delegate has recorded sign-off, and the sign-off sequence is evidenced in the audit trail.
column10:
The Detailed Design notes organisations vary on whether the report is signed before negotiations, before contract signature, or concurrently, but the audit trail must show the report was signed before the contract. Configuration point for FR-146.

CLIENT QUERY: The existing Notes already record that organisations vary on whether the evaluation report is signed before negotiations, before contract signature, or concurrently. Please confirm Intuitive Fusion's required sequence, noting the audit trail must always show the report was signed before the contract.

column3: The final, approved contract version shall route automatically into a contract-signing workflow, with a configurable review/approval chain prior to signing.
column7: Given an approved final contract version, when it is released for signature, then it enters the signing workflow automatically and each configured review/approval step must complete in order before signature is enabled.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the standard contract review/approval chain (roles and sequence) required before a contract routes to signing.

column3: Where a customer has no external legal system, the platform shall provide native legal matter management, comprising a legal kanban board, review-hour logging, and a clause library of corporate fallback positions and mandatory boilerplate.
column7: Given a tenant without an external legal system, when a matter is raised, then it appears on the legal kanban board, review hours can be logged against it, and clauses can be inserted from the clause library.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether Intuitive Fusion currently has an external legal matter management system, or will rely on the platform's native legal kanban/clause library capability — this determines whether the FR-0390 integration path is also required.

column3: Where a customer operates an enterprise legal platform (e.g. HighQ, Icertis), the system shall raise an outbound matter-initiation event through an integration gateway and synchronise redlines and matter-stage updates back to the procurement record via webhook in near real time.
column7: Given an integrated legal platform, when a matter is initiated, then the outbound event is delivered and acknowledged, and a subsequent redline or stage change in the legal platform is reflected against the procurement record without manual entry.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the specific external legal platform (if any) Intuitive Fusion's clients use today (e.g. HighQ, Icertis, or another), so the integration gateway can be scoped.

column3: The system shall provide a dynamic clause assembly engine that constructs a customised contract draft from project metadata (value, sector, risk tier, governing region), injecting mandatory government boilerplate for public-sector projects and appropriate IP protections for technology purchases.
column7: Given a public-sector technology procurement, when the draft is assembled, then mandatory government boilerplate and IP protection clauses are present, and the metadata that selected each clause is recorded.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm Intuitive Fusion's mandatory boilerplate clauses (government terms, IP protections, etc.) and the specific 'sector' and 'risk tier' categories that should drive automatic clause selection.

column3: The system shall monitor the negotiation room for material deviations to non-negotiable mandatory clauses (e.g. indemnity limits, liability caps, IP governance); a detected deviation shall block signature routing and force an approval loop to General Counsel or the risk delegate.
column7: Given a material deviation to a mandatory clause, when signature routing is attempted, then routing is blocked and an approval task is raised to General Counsel or the risk delegate, and only their approval releases the block.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the complete list of clauses Intuitive Fusion classifies as 'non-negotiable mandatory' beyond the examples given (indemnity limits, liability caps, IP governance), so the deviation monitor is configured correctly.

column3: During contract drafting, the system shall cross-check the winning supplier's tender submission against the original RFx and flag any inconsistencies (e.g. pricing, scope or terms that differ from what was tendered) for legal/procurement review before the draft proceeds.
column7: Given a winning submission that differs from the RFx on price, scope or terms, when the draft is assembled, then each inconsistency is itemised for review and the draft cannot proceed until every item is accepted or resolved.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether a detected inconsistency between the tender submission and RFx should hard-block contract drafting, or only flag for review while allowing drafting to proceed.

column3: The platform shall enforce signing-delegate authority separately from sourcing-approval authority, unlocking the final signature action only for user IDs holding valid legal execution delegation for the project's category and value.
column7: Given a user holding sourcing approval authority but not legal execution delegation, when they attempt to sign, then the signature action remains locked and the attempt is logged.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm Intuitive Fusion's legal execution delegation matrix (who may sign, by category and value) is available, distinct from the financial/sourcing DoA matrix requested at FR-0100.

column3: The system shall run a pre-flight verification of the vendor's legal name, tax registration and banking details against ERP/vetted records before signature options unlock.
column7: Given a vendor whose banking or tax details do not match the ERP/vetted record, when signature is requested, then signature options remain locked and the mismatch is reported for resolution.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the ERP or vetted record source this pre-flight vendor check should validate against, and the action to take (block versus warn) if a mismatch is found.

column3: The platform shall provide a native, eIDAS-aligned electronic/digital signature capability as a baseline, with interim or ongoing integration to third-party e-signature providers (e.g. DocuSign, Adobe Sign) supporting concurrent (any order) and sequential (defined order) multi-party signing.
column7: Given a contract requiring three signatories, when concurrent signing is selected, then all three can sign in any order; when sequential signing is selected, then each signatory is only invited after the preceding signature is recorded.
column10:
BRS §6.2 identifies native e-signature readiness as a delivery risk, with third-party integration as the interim path.

CLIENT QUERY: BRS §6.2 already flags native e-signature readiness as a delivery risk, with third-party integration as the interim path. Please confirm whether Intuitive Fusion will accept a third-party e-signature provider (DocuSign or Adobe Sign) as the primary signing method at go-live, with native signing following later.

column3: The platform shall support advanced signing workflows, including blind signing (a signatory signs without other parties' signatures or identities visible) and staged endorsement (signatures collected in a defined sequence of approval stages), with preset signature-block placement configurable within document templates.
column7: Given a template with preset signature blocks, when content is added and the document length changes, then the signature blocks remain correctly placed; and in blind signing, a signatory cannot see other parties' signatures or identities.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether blind signing (finance/legal endorsing before signatories see the document) is a standard requirement or an exception workflow for specific contract types.

column3: The signing capability shall extend to document types beyond the primary contract, including NDAs, confidentiality agreements and master agreements.
column7: Given an NDA, confidentiality agreement or master agreement, when it is routed for signature, then the same signing workflow, authority checks and audit trail apply as for a contract.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the complete list of document types (beyond NDA, confidentiality agreement, master agreement) that must support the same signing workflow.

column3: The platform shall support time-bound access grants for evaluation committee members, auditors and advisors, automatically revoking access to a project's documents at a configured expiry date or event (e.g. one month after contract signature, or on evaluation report sign-off).
column7: Given a time-bound grant with a configured expiry, when the expiry date or event is reached, then the user's access to that project's documents is revoked automatically and the revocation is logged.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the standard access-expiry trigger(s) Intuitive Fusion requires — a fixed period such as one month post-signature, an event such as evaluation report sign-off, or both depending on role.

column3: Where contract negotiations extend beyond 30 days, the platform shall automatically lock signature blocks and force a re-run of sanctions and financial risk checks on the counterparty before execution can proceed.
column7: Given negotiations open for more than 30 days, when signature is attempted, then signature blocks are locked until refreshed sanctions and financial risk checks have been completed and recorded.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the 30-day negotiation window drawn from the source design documents is the correct trigger for Intuitive Fusion, or specify a different period before signature blocks require a sanctions/risk re-check.

column3: The system shall send email invitations to internal and external signing delegates, with automated reminders where action has not been taken, shall allow signatories to view the full contract and raise questions before signing, and shall notify key stakeholders of signing progress.
column7: Given a signature request outstanding beyond the configured reminder interval, when the interval elapses, then a reminder is issued; and a signatory can view the full contract and raise a question against it before signing.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the required reminder cadence for outstanding signatory actions (e.g. daily, every two days) before further escalation.

column3: The system shall present an AI-generated, auto-populated summary of contract risks to the delegate ahead of signing, with legal retaining final review and edit before release.
column7: Given a contract ready for signature, when the delegate opens it, then an AI-generated risk summary is displayed, clearly labelled as AI-generated, and evidence of legal's final review is recorded.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the specific risk categories the AI-generated pre-signing summary must cover (e.g. clause deviations, insurance gaps, sanctions flags) beyond a general summary.

column3: Once signed, a contract shall be locked; deletion shall be restricted to authorised roles and shall always be logical (soft) rather than permanent, with the underlying record retained permanently in storage and recoverable.
column7: Given a signed contract, when an authorised role deletes it, then it is removed from the tenant's active view but the record is retained, recoverable and evidenced in the audit trail; unauthorised roles cannot delete it.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm which roles are authorised to soft-delete a signed contract record, and the approval step (if any) required before deletion.

column3: Contract variations shall be linked back to their originating (parent) contract record.
column7: Given a variation created against a contract, when either record is viewed, then the parent-child relationship is displayed and navigable in both directions.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether the parent-child link for contract variations should be visible/navigable from both the parent and the variation record, or from the parent only.

column3: Legal shall be able to collaborate in-platform and make live changes to the contract without a generate-edit-regenerate cycle, and shall be able to download final drafts or upload externally amended final drafts.
column7: Given a draft under legal review, when legal edits it in-platform, then the change is applied in place without regenerating the document; and an externally amended draft can be uploaded and adopted as the current version.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design, which identifies the generate-edit-regenerate cycle as unacceptable for legal users.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the specific document formats (native in-platform editor, Word round-trip, or both) legal users require for live contract editing.

column3: Legal shall be able to upload policies and historical legal advice for the AI to draw on when advising on deviations and negotiation positions.
column7: Given uploaded legal policies and historical advice, when AI deviation advice is requested, then the response draws on that corpus and cites the source document.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design. Must operate within the data-residency and closed-model constraints in NFR-R01 and SEC-D05

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the categories of historical legal advice Intuitive Fusion is willing to have ingested by the AI, noting this must stay within the data-residency and closed-model boundary already required at NFR-R01 and SEC-D05.

column3: The deviation register shall auto-populate a risk rating for each deviation, amendable by legal in plain language; users shall be able to ask what a deviation means; and the business or delegate shall be able to formally accept an identified risk.
column7: Given a deviation with an AI-assigned risk rating, when legal amends the rating in plain language, then the new rating is stored with the amendment attributed; and a delegate's formal risk acceptance is recorded against the deviation.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design; extends the structured deviation register in FR-025.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the risk-rating scale (e.g. Low/Medium/High, or numeric) the deviation register should use, and who has authority to formally 'accept' a risk on behalf of the business.

column3: The platform shall support an optional legal endorsement gate and optional endorsement by other business units (e.g. finance) before a contract is released for signing.
column7: Given a tenant with legal and finance endorsement gates enabled, when a contract is released for signing, then both endorsements must be recorded first; when the gates are disabled, then release proceeds without them.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design; configuration point for FR-146.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm which contract types or value tiers require the optional legal and/or finance endorsement gate to be mandatory rather than optional.

column3: The AI shall generate a negotiation strategy for the category, sector and procurement type, covering how to frame the negotiation, likely techniques, and a graduated set of positions — minimum expected result, expected outcome, very good outcome and stretch target — with recommended levers such as price, payment terms, limitation of liability and indemnities.
column7: Given a procurement in a known category, when a negotiation strategy is requested, then the strategy presents framing guidance, likely techniques and all four graduated positions with recommended levers, labelled as AI-generated.
column10:
Sourced from the Detailed Design; extends the negotiation recommendations in FR-059.

CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the source of 'category, sector and procurement type' benchmarking data for the AI-generated negotiation strategy — in-house historical outcomes, licensed market data, or both (the same dependency raised at FR-0295).

column3: Contract management records shall auto-populate from the executed contract directly for native contracts, or via AI extraction and parsing of supplier-provided PDF contracts, capturing obligations, pricing, SLAs, milestones, KPIs, deliverables, reviews, renewal dates, termination windows, liability caps and payment terms.
column7: Given an uploaded supplier PDF contract, when extraction completes, then obligations, SLAs, milestones, KPIs, key dates and commercial terms are populated into the contract management record with a confidence indicator and are user-amendable.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the expected accuracy/error-tolerance for AI extraction of obligations from supplier-provided PDF contracts, and the review step required before extracted data is relied upon operationally.

column3: Where a customer's ERP is integrated, the system shall enforce spend-ceiling guards that block purchase requisitions exceeding the contract limit.
column7: Given a contract at its authorised spend ceiling, when a purchase requisition exceeding the limit is raised, then the requisition is blocked and the contract owner is notified.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm which customer ERP(s) this spend-ceiling guard must integrate with at go-live (see also the ERP list requested at NFR-C02).

column3: The system shall perform automated line-item rate-card matching (3-way match) between purchase orders, contracts and invoices to block unapproved price increases.
column7: Given an invoice line priced above the contracted rate card, when the 3-way match runs, then the line is flagged and blocked from approval, identifying the contracted rate and the variance.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the tolerance threshold for a price variance to be treated as an 'unapproved price increase' — any variance, or a percentage/dollar tolerance band.

column3: The system shall provide an automated alert/notification engine covering SLAs, milestones, KPIs and optional-extension dates, including a configurable pre-expiry trigger (e.g. 90 days out) to the relevant contract managers/owners, via email and in-platform notification.
column7: Given a contract with a configured pre-expiry trigger, when the trigger date is reached, then the contract manager and owner receive both an email and an in-platform notification, and the despatch is logged.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the default pre-expiry alert lead time for Intuitive Fusion (90 days is given only as an example) and whether it should differ by contract value/risk tier.

column3: The platform shall implement non-negotiable, hard-coded system alerts that cannot be muted by users: a milestone countdown at 180, 90 and 60 days before expiry or extension close; an insurance-lapse warning 30 days before a compliance certificate expires; and spend-ceiling breach notices at 80%, 90% and 100% of the authorised limit.
column7: Given each defined system-alert threshold, when the threshold is met, then the alert is issued, and no user or administrator setting can suppress it.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the non-negotiable alert thresholds (180/90/60-day milestone countdown, 30-day insurance lapse warning, 80%/90%/100% spend-ceiling breach) drawn from the source design documents are acceptable as fixed platform defaults for Intuitive Fusion, since by definition these cannot be muted or reconfigured by users.

column3: The platform shall provide user-configurable custom milestone alerts, addable in plain language, with selectable delivery channels (in-app, email, SMS or Slack) and assigned owners.
column7: Given a user creating a custom alert in plain language, when it is saved, then the alert is scheduled with the nominated channel and owner, and fires at the specified time.
column10:
Conflict to resolve: BRS §3.9 lists SMS as an available channel for this release, while the Detailed Design lists SMS alerts as an optional future capability. Confirm whether SMS is in scope at go-live.

CLIENT QUERY: The existing Notes already flag a conflict: BRS §3.9 lists SMS as available for this release while the Detailed Design lists SMS as an optional future capability. Please confirm whether SMS alerting is required in scope at go-live.

column3: The system shall support rebate tracking against contracted rebate terms, automatically detecting and flagging missed or under-claimed rebates for follow-up.
column7: Given contracted rebate terms and actual spend, when the rebate check runs, then any missed or under-claimed rebate is flagged with the entitlement value and the shortfall.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm whether rebate terms will be captured as structured contract fields at authoring time, or must be extracted by AI from unstructured contract text.

column3: The system shall monitor price-escalation clauses (e.g. CPI-linked or scheduled increases) and flag supplier invoices that apply an escalation outside the contracted formula or schedule.
column7: Given a contract with a CPI-linked escalation clause, when an invoice applies an increase outside the contracted formula or timing, then the invoice line is flagged with the contracted basis and the calculated variance.
column10: CLIENT QUERY: Please confirm the specific escalation formats (CPI-linked, fixed % schedule, other) Intuitive Fusion's contracts typically use, so the AI extraction logic can be tuned.
